findings.title: PR #82 would remove the Associates tag from every product link, which the official text does not allow
findings.found: PR #82 (arena/359baa16-affil1) changes buy_url() so that a product without a validated Special Link is linked untagged. Program Policies §2(b) says a site must include the tag 'as a parameter in the URL of each link you place on your Site to an Amazon Site'. The current build tags every product link.
findings.why_it_matters: Read literally, an untagged Amazon link is itself outside §2(b). The gate the PR adds is a sound instinct about attribution, but it is applied to the wrong side: the policy asks for the tag, and the unconfirmed part is whether the tag belongs to an enrolled account.
findings.action: Not merged by this pass. Decision for the owner: keep the tag and confirm enrolment in Associates Central (FLG-002), or drop the tag and accept the policy reading above. Cross-scope request logged to arena/359baa16-affil1.

findings.title: The Affiliate launch checks workflow is red on main
findings.found: tools/sweep_surfaces.py --dry-run reports 'would move: 7 file(s)' under decision-support/ (editorial-plan, executive-summary, index, products, questions, suggestions, verification). The workflow requires 'would move: 0'. The run is recorded as failure on main (run 44686287239).
findings.why_it_matters: The Pages deployment is green, so the live site is not broken by this. The red check means the launch gate does not certify the published surface, which is the purpose the workflow states for itself.
findings.action: Not repaired here. PR #86 (arena/89ddabf5-affil1) and PR #84 (arena/771e5093-affil1) claim the launch gate and decision-support/. Owner decision: archive the seven files or add them to tools/build.py.

findings.title: Pages publishes the repository root, so the _config.yml exclude list does not apply
findings.found: The Pages API reports build_type 'legacy', source branch main, path '/'. The workflow's staging step (tools/stage.py into _site) is not the deployed artifact. The live site serves COORDINATION.md, src/data/product-intent.json, tools/build.py and archive/ (V-12, V-13, V-15, V-16). The repository ships a .nojekyll file (checked). _config.yml's exclude list is a Jekyll setting that the live root publication does not apply.
findings.why_it_matters: Files the repository's own exclude list names are public: the board, the register source, the build source and the archive README. Archived HTML carries noindex, which keeps it out of search results but does not stop it being served.
findings.action: Not changed. Owner decision: keep the root publication and accept it, or publish from a staged artifact (the workflow's 'workflow' source) so the staging step decides what is public.

findings.title: The supplied tracking ID does not match the example format in the policy
findings.found: Program Policies §2(b) gives the tag format as 'XXXXX-##, or such other format as we may designate'. The supplied ID is shopnow047c-20, which is not in the XXXXX-## example form.
findings.why_it_matters: The policy allows other formats, so this is not evidence the ID is wrong. It is one more reason to confirm the ID in Associates Central before any link is trusted.
findings.action: Confirm the ID in Associates Central (FLG-002). This pass does not treat the format as a defect.

findings.title: Two summary documents state counts that no longer match the build
findings.found: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md says '29 pages' and '19 flags'. The build produces 30 generated pages before this pass and the flag register holds 22 entries. README.md links to /sources/ and /flagged/, which are not generated; the flagged page is /review/.
findings.why_it_matters: A reader who follows the summary lands on a count that is wrong, or a link that is dead.
findings.action: EXECUTIVE_SUMMARY.md is not rewritten in this pass: the rewrite is outside the narrowed claim. Logged as a request for the integration session, with the current counts computed from src/data: 30 generated pages before this pass, 22 flags.

findings.title: The paid-link gate's own unit test fails on main, and no workflow runs it
findings.found: tools/test_paid_link_gate.py asserts that public observations create no tags (approved_amazon_urls() == {}). On this base the assertion fails: layout.approved_amazon_urls() returns a tagged URL for all five ASINs, because layout.py falls back to the supplied tag. None of the four workflows in .github/workflows/ runs tools/test_paid_link_gate.py or any unittest suite under tools/.
findings.why_it_matters: The test states the rule PR #82 implements. Against the current build it is red, and nothing reports that. A gate that is never run does not gate.
findings.action: Not changed in this pass: the fix belongs with the RVW-01 decision. Once the owner decides which rule stands, the test should be made to match it and added to a workflow.
